misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Execution Engine is an internal component of the EVM, not an external entity. It produces logs as part of internal state transitions, not as external input.
Calling Contract is another smart contract within the same EVM execution context. It is internal to the system, not external. Contracts calling precompiles is an internal operation.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External client querying for logs via eth_getLogs or similar RPC methods. Clients are anonymous network connections. Query parameters must be validated to prevent resource exhaustion attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: Debugging/Analysis Tool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External tool that configures tracing to capture EVM execution details. Typically authenticated via node access controls (RPC auth, local socket). However, tracer implementations could impact performance or leak sensitive data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/Signer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External wallet or signing mechanism that creates and signs transactions. User-installed and user-controlled. Trusted for key management but transaction data must still be validated by the network.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Broadcaster
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External entity submitting signed transactions to the network. Could be any network participant. Transaction signatures and content must be fully validated regardless of source.

trusted_external_entities.name: Replay Attacker
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Explicitly malicious actor attempting to replay transactions across chains. This is a threat model entity representing adversarial behavior. All inputs must be validated as if from an attacker.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Log query parameters from clients must be validated. Overly broad queries could cause resource exhaustion. Rate limiting should be applied.
Debugging tool provides tracer implementation. Access should be restricted to authorized operators. Tracer code could impact performance or access sensitive execution data.
Wallet creates transaction with chain ID for replay protection. User trusts wallet for key security, but network validates all transaction fields independently.
Signed transactions from any broadcaster must have signature validated, chain ID verified, and all fields checked against consensus rules.
Attacker observes and captures transactions from public chain. This is the threat model - EIP-155 chain ID protection prevents replay by binding signatures to specific chains.
